idiom_name: ring buffer + pthread_mutex_t/pthread_cond_t pair (or a POSIX message queue)
implementation_notes: C has queue primitives but no queue abstraction, so the classic structure is written by hand: a statically allocated ring buffer of fixed capacity, one pthread_mutex_t guarding head/tail/length, and two pthread_cond_t - not_full (producers wait) and not_empty (workers wait). Producers block in while (len == CAP) pthread_cond_wait(&not_full, &m), so the buffer bound is the backpressure and a burst is stored rather than dropped. Workers run the same loop on not_empty and process outside the critical section. This remains the honest default because nothing in the C runtime manages queue capacity, worker lifetime or acknowledgement for you.
pitfalls: pthread_cond_wait can wake spuriously, so the condition must be re-tested in a while loop - an if silently overruns the buffer.
With several consumers, signal wakes only one waiter; choosing signal vs broadcast incorrectly leaves workers parked with work in the queue.
A queue built as a malloc'd unbounded linked list has no bound and is the failure mode the pattern exists to prevent.
Mixing a condition variable with non-atomic length/head/tail updates without holding the mutex is a data race even when the values look correct.

variants.name: POSIX message queue as the buffer (mq_open/mq_send/mq_receive)
variants.implementation_notes: A POSIX message queue (librt, <mqueue.h>) moves the buffer into the kernel: mq_open creates it with mq_maxmsg messages of mq_msgsize bytes each, mq_send blocks by default once the queue holds mq_maxmsg messages, and mq_receive blocks until one is available. That gives the bound and the blocking hand-off for free and can be shared between processes on the same host, at the cost of fixed-size messages and no worker management: the consumer loop, acknowledgement and dead-letter handling are still yours.
pitfalls: mq_send defaults to blocking (the desired policy); with O_NONBLOCK set it fails with EAGAIN, which must be handled as the shed path rather than ignored.
Messages are fixed-size byte blocks with no type safety; the payload layout must be versioned by hand.
The queue lives in the kernel and persists until mq_unlink, so a crashed producer's backlog is still there - and so is a queue that was never cleaned up.
